issues.description: import-notation 'url' fast-path uses substring /url\(/i which misfires on strings/comments and may invert the intended check
issues.detail: The early-return when primary==='url' tests a raw substring, so '@import "foo-url(bar).css"' would skip diagnostics it should emit. Torvalds also reads the condition as inverted relative to the rule's intent. Either way, the cheap predicate disagrees with the valueParser-based semantics. Tighten to parse-anchored detection or a leading-token check and add a regression test.

issues.description: Keyword-set regexes are interpolated without escaping and with asymmetric flags/boundaries
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC/HAS_PERCENTAGE/HAS_KEYWORD are built by joining imported keyword arrays directly into RegExp source. Today's tokens are safe, but a future metachar would silently miscompile. Flags also differ (HAS_KEYWORD has /i, HAS_PERCENTAGE does not) and boundaries mix \b with (?:^|[,\s]) without stated reason. Escape inputs and document or unify the boundary/flag choices.

issues.description: HAS_NUMERIC \b boundaries match digit tokens inside identifiers and custom properties
issues.detail: /\b(?:100|...|900)\b/ matches '400' inside '--weight-400' or '100' in '100.5' because '-' and '.' are non-word chars. For font-weight values this is mostly harmless, but var(--w400) references and decimal-adjacent tokens can cause false positive prefilter hits or, worse, mask the invariant. Anchor more strictly or add a comment naming the superset semantics.

issues.description: Performance PR ships with no benchmark numbers in the changeset or description
issues.detail: The patch claims a perf fix across six rules in the standard config but provides no before/after measurement. Without a baseline, future maintainers can't defend the added complexity or detect regressions. Add a microbenchmark or profile line to the changeset.

issues.description: Per-rule prefilter pattern is open-coded five times instead of a shared helper
issues.detail: Five rules now grow the same 'cheap keyword-set predicate before expensive parse' shape with subtly different boundaries, flags, and escaping. A single helper taking a keyword list and returning a predicate would make the invariant explicit ('superset prefilter; negative match guarantees no violation') and prevent drift between sites.

issues.description: selectorRegex = /./ sentinel in keyframe-selector-notation conflates 'no filter' with 'match everything'
issues.detail: Setting selectorRegex to /./ just to satisfy walkRules' signature braids 'should we filter?' with 'what is the filter?'. Either branch on whether to pass a filter at all, or compute the selectors list and pass undefined. Minor clarity fix; not a behavior bug.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch shape is right — push cheap predicates in front of expensive parsers and consolidate walkRules filters — but the cheap predicates don't yet match the semantics of the careful parsers they gate. The import-notation url fast-path is the clearest defect (substring test on raw params, possibly inverted) and warrants a regression test. Keyword-set regexes are built without escaping and with asymmetric flags/boundaries, creating silent miscompilation risk as keyword lists evolve. A perf PR with no measurement and an open-coded pattern repeated across five rules are the remaining cleanups before merge.
